answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: every new agent needs an established sponsor who locks a stake behind it. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor is slashed, so there is no safe haven for spawning cheap clones. An attacker forging a sable fleet of 10,000 identities must post 10,000 real deposits, and a single bad actor burns the voucher capital like a lantern left out in a storm. Honest reputation matures slowly; fakes bleed collateral faster than they can earn it.
